budget.qualification: GOAL section 4 requires React updates outside the render loop; PLAN records 9.7-14.3 ms mean CPU on 62 buildings, not a hard frame limit. No numeric streaming budget was found in those two documents. The engine explicitly reserves most of a 16.7 ms frame; 100 ms is the task/REH11 floor, not a smooth-frame claim.

trace.finding: onView dispatched workspace setTick after every rendered frame, repeating layer-list/notes/label/inspector reconciliation even when only the camera or one part moved. WindowedArea had the same pattern.

Footprint conversion is memoised; setBuildings reconciles inputs and drains new geometry in existing 4 ms slices. The 1661 meshes are not all constructed by one setter call. Existing merged pad batches and materials were retained.

SSE invalidates the existing manifest query; SurfaceParts retains part objects. Artifact hashes are checked and TIFF/LAS decoding is already in a worker with transferred buffers. Canvas creation, React publication, point scene-axis conversion and GPU uploads remain on the main thread.

Existing surface objects were already retained by identity, but all available new parts were built synchronously and first uploaded together. TilesRenderer.update remains in the imperative frame; no 3D Tiles changes were needed for these TIFF/LAS parts.

comparison.qualification: Before count was observed by the failing regression on the base implementation. After timings are one Node run of real Three.js builders with a fake renderer/canvas boundary, not browser frames or GPU upload time. No before wall-time speedup is claimed. Deterministic work-count assertions, not noisy wall-clock thresholds, gate the regression.

footprintCheck.qualification: Confirms the existing chunk budget and no dropped buildings; fake time excludes pads, drawing and browser work.
